words.example: The doctor gave me medicine for my cold.

words.description: A mix is different things put together.
words.example: The green mix we made in science class spilled onto the table.

words.description: To organize is to plan or get ready for an event.
words.example: Make a list to help you organize the things you need.

words.description: A period is an amount of time when something happens.
words.example: In one period in Europe, there were many knights.

words.description: If people populate an area, they live there.
words.example: Billions of people populate the Earth.

words.description: To produce something is to make or grow it.
words.example: This tree produces apples every year.

words.description: A range is a number or a set of similar things.
words.example: I saw a range of cars to choose from.

words.description: To recognize something is to know it because you have seen it before.
words.example: I recognized an old friend from many years ago.

words.description: If something is regular , it happens often and in equal amounts of time.
words.example: Our regular lunch time is around noon.

words.description: A sign is a notice giving information, directions, a warning, etc.
words.example: The sign indicated that today would be a bad day.

words.description: A tip is a pointed end of something.
words.example: The tip of his pen was very sharp.

words.description: A tradition is something people have been doing for a long time.
words.example: Marriage is a tradition all over the world.

words.description: Trash is waste material or unwanted or worthless things.
words.example: Please take out the trash ; it smells bad.

words.description: If something is wide , it is large from side to side.
words.example: The door was as wide as my arms.

words.description: Advice is an opinion about what to do.
words.example: I don’t know how to study for my exams. Can you give me some advice ?

words.description: Along means to move from one part of a road, river, etc. to another.
words.example: Walk along this tunnel for ten minutes, and you’ll see a door on the left.

words.description: Attention is the notice, thought, or consideration of someone.
words.example: His work got the attention of two of his co-workers.

words.description: To attract means to make a person or thing come closer or be interested.
words.example: The magnet attracted the metal.

words.description: To climb means to use your hands and feet to go up on something.
words.example: The girls climbed to the top of the mountain.

words.description: To drop is to fall or allow something to fall.
words.example: A small amount of water dropped from the bottle.

words.description: If something is final , it is the last part.
words.example: In the final part of the film, the man and the woman got married.

words.description: Further is used to say something is from a distance or time.
words.example: The escalator is further along than I thought.

words.description: To imply something is to suggest it without saying it.
words.example: The man implied that he wanted the job, but he didn’t say so.

words.description: To maintain means to make something stay the same.
words.example: The balls maintain constant movement.

words.description: You use neither to connect two negative statements.
words.example: Neither the pass on the left nor the pass on the right will lead us home.

words.description: Otherwise means different or in another way.
words.example: It’s good to stay active; otherwise , you’ll gain weight.

words.description: If something is physical , it is related to your body and not your mind.
words.example: Biking is good for your physical health.

words.description: To prove something is to show that it is true.
words.example: My teacher proved the answer on the board.

words.description: To react is to act in a certain way because of something that happened.
words.example: James reacted badly to the news.

words.description: To ride something is to travel on it. You can ride an animal, a bike, etc.
words.example: I will ride a roller-coaster for the first time today.

words.description: If something is situated somewhere, it is in that place.
words.example: The white board is situated between the two men.

words.description: Society is people and the way that they live.
words.example: Society expects people to be good and honest.

words.description: A standard is what people consider normal or good.
words.example: This older model TV is below our store’s standards .

words.description: To suggest something means to give an idea or plan about it.
words.example: He suggested that we go to see his boss.

words.description: Actually means in fact or really.
words.example: My dad looks a little mean, but actually he’s very kind.

words.description: Bite is the act of using your teeth to cut and tear into something.
words.example: The boy took a big bite out of his hamburger.

words.description: The coast is the land by an ocean.
words.example: I stayed on the southern coast of Australia.

words.description: A deal is an agreement that you have with another person.
words.example: I made a deal with the other company to give us some money.

words.description: The desert is an area of land without many plants or water.
words.example: Not many plants grow in the desert .

words.description: An earthquake is a shaking movement of the ground.
words.example: The building shook during the earthquake .

words.description: If something is effective , it works well.
words.example: Swimming is an effective way to stay healthy.

words.description: To examine something is to look at it carefully.
words.example: The doctor examined my eyes today.

words.description: If something is false , it is not correct.
words.example: If you think the answer is false , press the red button.

words.description: A gift is something you give someone.
words.example: Dave received many gifts for Christmas.

words.description: Hunger is the feeling that you get when you need to eat.
words.example: After playing all day long, he was filled with hunger .

words.description: To imagine something is to think of it in your mind.
words.example: Sally imagined herself winning lots of money.

words.description: A journey is a long trip.
words.example: I went on a journey across the country with my parents.

words.description: A puzzle is something that is hard to understand.
words.example: The question was a puzzle to him.

words.description: Quite is used to say that something is complete or very much.
words.example: I think typing on a keyboard is quite easy.

words.description: Rather is used when you want to do one thing but not the other.
words.example: I would rather have the red one than the blue one.

words.description: If something is specific , it is precise or exact.
words.example: Please choose a specific place on the map.

words.description: A tour is a short trip in which you see many sights.
words.example: I took a tour of Asia and Europe.

words.description: A trip is a journey to a certain place.
words.example: Ken took a trip to the city yesterday.

words.description: If something has value , it is worth a lot of money.
words.example: Matthew found a treasure of very high value .

words.description: A band is a group of people who play music.
words.example: My brother is in a rock band .

words.description: Barely means by the smallest amount, almost not.
words.example: I barely had enough money to pay for my bus ticket.

words.description: If something is boring , it is not fun.
words.example: I think the Internet is boring .

words.description: To cancel means to decide that an event or a request will not happen.
words.example: She cancelled the rest of her plans because of the rain.

words.description: A driveway is a short private road that leads to a person’s home.
words.example: The long driveway led us to their new house.

words.description: Garbage is waste material like unwanted or spoiled food, bottles, paper, etc.
words.example: The boy cleaned up the garbage around his house.

words.description: An instrument is something designed to do a certain task like music.
words.example: My favorite musical instrument is the piano.

words.description: A list is a record of information printed with an item on each line.
words.example: My mom makes a list of groceries to buy.

words.description: Magic is the power to do impossible things.
words.example: The magician used magic to pull a rabbit out of his hat.

words.description: A message is a set of words that you send to someone.
words.example: I left a message for you in the envelope.

words.description: To notice something is to see it for the first time.
words.example: Did you notice the view?

words.description: To own something means to have it. That thing belongs to you.
words.example: My grandfather owns that house.

words.description: To predict something is to say that it will happen.
words.example: She predicted that I would get married next year.

words.description: A professor is a person who teaches in college.
words.example: Mike’s science professor knows a lot about physics.

words.description: To rush is to go somewhere or do something very quickly.
words.example: Nancy rushed to finish her homework.

words.description: A schedule is a plan that tells you when to do things.
words.example: What is your class schedule for today?

words.description: To share something is to give some of it to another person.
words.example: Jimmy shared his apple with me.

words.description: A stage is a place where actors or musicians act or sing.
words.example: A large screen was on the stage .

words.description: A storm is very bad weather. There is a lot of rain or snow.
words.example: Did that storm wake you up last night?

words.description: You use within to say that something is inside another thing.
words.example: Within the box, there was a pizza.

words.description: To advertise is to tell people about something on TV, radio, etc.
words.example: They used a rabbit to help them advertise their product.

words.description: To assign something to someone is to tell them to do it.
words.example: I assigned the worker an important task.

words.description: An audience is a group of people who watch something together.
words.example: There was a large audience at the game.

words.description: Breakfast is the first meal of the day.
words.example: I eat breakfast at 8:00 every morning.

words.description: A competition is a contest to see who is the best at something.
words.example: He won the running competition over the weekend.

words.description: If the weather is cool , it is a little bit cold.
words.example: The weather is cool in the fall.

words.description: If you gain something, you get more of it.
words.example: I gained some weight over the summer.

words.description: Importance means the quality or condition of being needed or valued.
words.example: VIPs are people of great importance .

words.description: Knowledge is information that you have about something.
words.example: A music teacher should have good knowledge of music.

words.description: If something is major , it is big or important.
words.example: I have a major problem. My boss wants me to redo my project!

words.description: Mean describes someone who is unkind or cruel.
words.example: My co-worker is a very mean person. He gets angry very quickly.

words.description: If you prefer something, you want it more than something else.
words.example: I prefer to take the path that will lead me to a bright future.

words.description: A president is the leader of a country.
words.example: The president of our country made an important announcement.

words.description: Progress is the act of getting closer to doing or finishing something.
words.example: Our company made financial progress this year.

words.description: Respect is a good opinion of someone because they are good.
words.example: I have great respect for firemen.

words.description: Ifyou are rich , you have a lot of money.
words.example: He’s rich . He can buy anything he wants.

words.description: A skill is the knowledge and ability that allows you to do something well.
words.example: A snowboarder must have the right skills to do well.

words.description: Somehow means in a way or by some means which is not known.
words.example: He somehow had to find a way to reach the life preserver.

words.description: Strength is the physical power that you have.
words.example: Exercising will increase your strength and give you more power.

words.description: To vote is to officially choose between two or more things.
words.example: I voted for Billy to be our class president.

words.description: If something is above , it is at a higher level than something else.
words.example: He straightened the sign that was above the crowd.

words.description: If something is ahead of something else, it is in front of it.
words.example: The blue car drove on ahead of us.

words.description: An amount is how much there is of something.
words.example: Can I use my card to pay for the entire amount ?

words.description: A belief is a strong feeling that something is correct or true.
words.example: A preacher or priest should have a strong belief in God.

words.description: The center of something is the middle of it.
words.example: The center of a dart board is the most important spot.

words.description: If something is common , it happens often or there is much of it.
words.example: It is common for snow to fall in the winter.

words.description: To cost is to require expenditure or payment.
words.example: These designer shoes cost more than the regular ones.

words.description: To demonstrate something is to show how it is done.
words.example: She demonstrated her plan to her co-workers.

words.description: Different describes someone or something that is not the same as others.
words.example: Each of my sisters has a different hair style from one another.

words.description: Evidence is a fact or thing that you use to prove something.
words.example: He used the pictures as evidence that UFOs are real.

words.description: Honesty means the quality of being truthful or honest.
words.example: A courtroom should be a place of honesty .

words.description: An idiom is a phrase with a meaning different from its words.
words.example: The idiom “when pigs fly” means that something will never happen.

words.description: If something is independent , it is not controlled by something else.
words.example: She chose to live an independent life in the country.

words.description: Inside means the inner part, space or side of something.
words.example: The inside of the box was empty.

words.description: A master is a person who is very good at something.
words.example: My brother is a master of taekwondo.

words.description: A memory is something you remember.
words.example: The memory of my first time in the city will always be the best.

words.description: If something is proper , it is right.
words.example: It is not proper to throw your garbage on the road.

words.description: To scan something is to look at it very carefully.
words.example: You must scan each person closely.

words.description: A section is a part of something larger.
words.example: The green section of the graph is the most important part.

words.description: The surface of something is the top part or outside of it.
words.example: The surface of the moon is very rough.
